answer: PoA makes each identity’s bonded escrow an anchor: when k identities equivocate in a correlated event, penalties grow as O(k²), reflecting pairwise coordination rather than merely counting claims. Detection applies an additional capital-loss multiplier such as e^(αk), with α set by protocol rules, so a sybil swarm risks sharply greater forfeiture. An inlet for new identities therefore does not bypass the ridge of correlated-evidence checks or the asymmetric depreciation of slashed collateral.
